Our Story

Nobody calls it Leo’s. Everybody calls it Mama’s.

The shop was founded by the Leo family and carried for decades by Nancy “Mama” DeBenedittis — so beloved that when she passed in 2009, the city named the street and the nearby school for her. Her daughters Irene and Marie run it today: Irene makes the mozzarella, Marie does the cooking, and neither uses a recipe.

The walls tell the rest — decades of photos, mayors, and Mets. This is the pregame ritual before Citi Field: stop on 104th Street, get a hero wrapped in Leo’s paper, and bring Corona with you to the game.

First time in? Say so. You’ll probably leave with a warm taste of fresh mozzarella and a sandwich you’ll be telling people about.
